headline: Carr's four touchdowns lift Notre Dame past USC in defensive struggle
body: Notre Dame's offense found its rhythm when it mattered most, with quarterback CJ Carr orchestrating a methodical performance that overwhelmed USC despite the Trojans keeping pace statistically. Carr's four touchdown passes on 23 completions gave the visiting defense room to operate, and they did, with linebacker Lucas recording 15 tackles to set the tone up front. The numbers tell a story of efficiency meeting execution: Notre Dame's passing attack netted 283 yards while USC generated 277, yet the gap in the final score reflected something deeper than raw yardage.

The turning point arrived in USC's inability to capitalize on possessions that should have yielded more. Moss completed 23 of 40 passes and found Ford downfield for 98 receiving yards, but the Trojans managed only 16 points from their efforts. A fumble late in the game crystallized the difference—possession after possession, Notre Dame's offense converted while USC's stalled. The defensive unit for Notre Dame, anchored by Lucas's workmanlike performance, never allowed the Trojans to string together the kind of drive that would break the game open.

This was a game decided not by highlight reel plays but by the accumulation of small advantages. Carr and Notre Dame's coaching room found a formula: get the ball to Southall on the perimeter where he could operate, attack vertically with confidence, and let the defense manage possessions. USC had moments—Ford's 98 yards showed the explosive potential was there—but consistency eluded them when it counted. Notre Dame leaves with a decisive 12-point victory that feels more convincing than the total yards suggest.
turningPoint: USC's fumble in the fourth quarter came at a moment when the Trojans were within striking distance, and Notre Dame's offense responded with a scoring drive that essentially sealed the game.

unsungHero.name: Shaw
unsungHero.why: The defensive end compiled five tackles in a losing effort and was one of few bright spots on a unit that couldn't consistently pressure Carr, yet his work often went unnoticed amid the offensive struggles.
